title: Examining the robustness of LLM evaluation to the distributional assumptions of benchmarks

paper.repo_note: No code or data release found in the paper (no GitHub/Drive link; only HF dataset links for ANLI). Several evaluated models are Microsoft/OpenAI-internal names (Text-Alpha-002-Current, DV3-FP8, Babbage-0721, ChatGPT-Turbo-Base-0516, ChatGPT-202301).

dependence.note: The analysed objects are per-prompt correctness vectors of 12-14 LLMs per benchmark; the finding (non-random correlation structure, ranking changes under reweighting) is a property of that model set's outputs.

claim.statement: Per-prompt performance vectors across LLMs are non-randomly correlated: clustering observed performance vectors yields higher average silhouette scores than permuted vectors (ANLI 0.52 vs 0.21, HellaSwag 0.54 vs 0.24, CommonsenseQA 0.61 vs 0.29, CNN/DM 0.25 vs 0.21; Table 3), and permutation / KS tests reject random structure (KS p = 2e-5 on ANLI, HS, CSQA; Table 2); consequently prompt reweighting changes model rankings (Sec. 5.2).
claim.metric: Average silhouette score (spherical k-means, cosine distance, k chosen to maximise silhouette) of prompt performance vectors vs a random permutation; permutation-test p-values on Hamming/cosine/Jaccard correlations (average, 75th, 95th percentile) and KS test
claim.original_source: Paper Tables 2 and 3 (Sec. 5.1); model list Table 1 (Sec. 4.3); test sizes Sec. 4.4

protocol.model: Model set per benchmark (Table 1), 12 (ANLI) / 13 (HS) / 14 (CSQA) / 8 (CNN/DM) models: GPT-4-0314, GPT-4-0613 (Chat), GPT-4-Turbo-1106 (Chat) and GPT-4-Turbo-1106 (completion) = gpt-4-1106-preview, ChatGPT-Turbo-0301/0613, Text-Davinci-002/003, DaVinci, Llama-13B/30B/65B, Llama-2-13B/70B, Claude-2, Falcon-180b, Koala-13B, Vicuna-13B, Mistral-7B, Alpaca-7B, Persimmon-8B, plus internal models. gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 was NOT used: 'GPT-4-Turbo' here is the 1106 preview.
protocol.model_status: dead (gpt-4-1106-preview 2026-03-26; gpt-4-0314/0613, gpt-3.5-turbo-0301/0613, text-davinci-002/003, claude-2 all dead). Live arm not an experimental arm.
protocol.endpoint: not reported (mix of OpenAI API, internal endpoints and local GPUs)
protocol.prompt_source: not available (few-shot format not given; ANLI 7-shot from dev set, HellaSwag 10-shot, CSQA 5-shot, CNN/DM 5-shot)
protocol.n_items: ANLI test 1,200; HellaSwag 1,005; CommonsenseQA 1,221; CNN/DM 1,150 (10% random test splits for the last three, split not released)
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: accuracy per prompt (binary) or ROUGE, then clustering + permutation tests + reweighting analysis (code not released).

artifacts.data_license: benchmarks themselves are public (ANLI CC BY-NC 4.0, HellaSwag MIT, CommonsenseQA MIT, CNN/DM research use); the performance matrices, splits and prompts are not released
artifacts.notes: The claim concerns a specific set of models, several of which never existed outside Microsoft; the set cannot be reconstituted by anyone.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm: 'GPT-4-Turbo-1106' = gpt-4-1106-preview (dead); no dying model in Table 1
no code, prompts, random test splits or performance matrices released
several evaluated models are internal (Text-Alpha-002-Current, DV3-FP8, Babbage-0721, ChatGPT-Turbo-Base-0516) - unavailable to external researchers
the claim is a property of the model *set*; replacing individual models changes the object of study
decoding parameters and few-shot prompt formats unreported

successors: a successor re-execution would need a fresh panel of >=12 models (gpt-5 family, claude, gemini, llama, qwen, plus open checkpoints) and would test whether the structural finding generalises, not whether the original panel drifted

full_hypothetical.note: Not estimable as a re-execution: requires >=12 models. Per single closed-model run: 4,576 items x ~1,500 few-shot input tokens = 6.9M in + ~0.1M out -> ~75 USD per gpt-4-turbo model; a 12-model panel mixing API and open models ~300-500 USD API spend plus GPU time.

representative_subset.note: ANLI only (1,200 items, 12 models) would be the smallest faithful unit; still needs a full model panel

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1: survival = observed silhouette > permuted silhouette with permutation p < 0.05 on the same benchmark (direction + significance); partial = direction holds but not significant; dead = no difference. Applicable only to a successor panel.
judgment.notes: Not executable; recorded for the census as dependence=subject, artifacts=none.

status_reason: live model not an experimental arm (only gpt-4-1106-preview and older, all dead); no artifacts; internal models in the panel
